plants.name: Syringa vulgaris
plants.description: A deciduous shrub with dense, conical clusters of intensely fragrant flowers. Widely cultivated in gardens and often naturalized along old homesteads and roadsides in cool temperate regions.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid to late spring (April to May in the Northern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Temperate North America, Europe, and northern Asia; native to the Balkan Peninsula
plants.funFact: Lilac is a member of the olive family (Oleaceae), and its fragrance has been used in perfumery for centuries.

plants.name: Paeonia lactiflora
plants.description: A long-lived herbaceous perennial with large, showy, often fragrant blooms and glossy, deeply lobed foliage. Early cultivars open in mid-May in many temperate gardens.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring to early summer (May to June)
plants.location: Native to Siberia, Mongolia, and northern China; cultivated worldwide in temperate climates
plants.funFact: Peonies can live and flower for more than 50 years in the same spot, and ants visiting the buds feed on nectar but are not needed for blooming.

plants.name: Wisteria sinensis
plants.description: A vigorous, twining woody vine producing pendulous racemes of fragrant, pea-like flowers that cascade from pergolas, walls, and trees, often blooming before the leaves fully emerge.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid-spring to early summer (April to May)
plants.location: Native to China; widely cultivated in Europe, North America, and Japan
plants.funFact: Wisteria vines twine counterclockwise in Chinese wisteria, whereas Japanese wisteria twines clockwise, and some old specimens have lived over 100 years.

plants.name: Jacaranda mimosifolia
plants.description: A tropical to subtropical tree with fern-like leaves and spectacular panicles of trumpet-shaped flowers. In the Northern Hemisphere tropics and subtropics such as Mexico and parts of Florida and India, it blooms heavily around this time.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring (May to June in the Northern Hemisphere subtropics); October to November in the Southern Hemisphere
plants.location: Native to South America (Argentina, Bolivia); planted in Mexico, southern USA, South Africa, Australia, and India
plants.funFact: In Pretoria, South Africa, so many jacarandas are planted that the city is nicknamed the Jacaranda City, though the trees there bloom in October.
